title: Justifying application extends to practical use of the whole divine Word
source_text: CXIV. Et ita quoque ad eorum sententiam accedo qui censent applicationem illam, quae justificantis fidei propria est, & per quam ab historica & mortua fide distinguitur, non esse restringendam ad illam persuasionem, per quam aliquis credit bona Evangelio promissa ad se pertinere, nec etiam ad illam fiduciam perfugii, qua quis in Deum recumbit, tanquam in authorem salutis, ut a malis suis liberetur, & bona salutaria a Deo consequatur; sed illam extendendam esse ad practicam totius Verbi Divini considerationem, per quam fit ut homo fidelis singulas ejus partes ad peculiarem suum usum referat, nempe ad minas contremiscens, & mandatis obsequens, & spem suam in divinis promissionibus figens; ac denique ex mysteriis redemptionis nostrae materiam consolationis, gratitudinis, & amoris erga Deum hauriens.
pass_a_gloss: And so I also come over to the opinion of those who hold that that application which is proper to justifying faith, and by which it is distinguished from historical and dead faith, is not to be restricted to that persuasion by which someone believes the goods promised in the Gospel pertain to him, nor even to that refuge-trust by which one reclines upon God as author of salvation, that he may be freed from his evils and obtain saving goods from God; but that it is to be extended to the practical consideration of the whole divine Word, through which it comes about that the believing person refers each of its parts to his own peculiar use — namely trembling at threats, obeying commandments, and fixing his hope in the divine promises; and finally drawing from the mysteries of our redemption matter for consolation, gratitude, and love toward God.
pass_b_english: I also side with those who refuse to restrict justifying faith's distinctive application to either grace-persuasion or refuge-trust alone.
Extend it to practical consideration of the whole Word: trembling at threats, obeying commands, fixing hope on promises, and drawing consolation, gratitude, and love from redemption's mysteries.
